title_candidates: Hugging Face Jobs makes temporary vLLM servers easier to try
summary: Hugging Face showed how to launch a temporary vLLM OpenAI-compatible server on HF Jobs, useful for quick model tests without long-lived infrastructure.

primary_source.title: Run a vLLM Server on HF Jobs in One Command
primary_source.author: Hugging Face
key_facts: Hugging Face published a guide for running vLLM servers on HF Jobs.
The guide uses hf jobs run with the official vllm/vllm-openai image and an exposed port.
The resulting endpoint is OpenAI API compatible and requires an HF token for access.
Jobs are billed per second and should be stopped when testing is done.

steps.instruction: Sign in with the HF CLI and check available hardware before launching anything.
Choose a small model first, such as the guide's Qwen3-4B example, and set a short timeout.
Launch the job, copy the exposed endpoint, and test the models endpoint with your HF token.
Send one short chat-completion request and confirm the output matches the selected model.
Cancel the job immediately after testing so you do not keep paying for idle GPU time.

references.title: Run a vLLM Server on HF Jobs in One Command

risk_flags: This guide involves paid GPU jobs; article tells users to start small and cancel explicitly.
